title: HighDimensionalSeparableNoiseLinfSmooth.lean

problem_class.label: nonconvex
problem_class.details: The objective may be any differentiable function on ℝᵈ satisfying the stated gradient smoothness bound and having a finite infimum f⋆ with f(x₀)−f⋆ ≤ Δ. The infimum need not be attained.
problem_class.evidence: LongTails/Setups/SeparableNoiseLinfSmooth.lean, spec.admissible (gradient, lower bound, approximation of fstar, and initial gap).

oracle.label: stochastic_gradient
oracle.details: Each call at x returns one full vector g(x,ξ) with mean ∇f(x). The oracle uses a fresh i.i.d. real seed on each call. The algorithm receives the vector alone and may query adaptively using its own independent randomness. The public inputs are d, L, S, Δ, ε, and x₀. The objective, oracle map, seed law, and infimum are hidden.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/HighDimensionalSeparableNoiseLinfSmooth.lean, Params, toGeneral, and spec.publicInput; LongTails/Setups/SeparableNoiseLinfSmooth.lean, spec.admissible; LongTails/Setups/StochasticGeneralizedSmoothAndConvex.lean, IID; LongTails/Template.lean, Algorithm, Setup.allowedAlgorithm, and Convergence.

distinctive_assumptions.label: bounded_variance
distinctive_assumptions.details: At every x, the sum of coordinate standard deviations satisfies ∑ᵢ (𝔼[(gᵢ(x,ξ)−∂ᵢf(x))²])¹ᐟ² ≤ S. The sum is taken at the same x before imposing the uniform bound. Coordinates within a reply may be dependent.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/SeparableNoiseLinfSmooth.lean, spec.admissible (coordinate second-moment integrability and sum of square roots).

distinctive_assumptions.label: non_euclidean_geometry
distinctive_assumptions.details: The gradient is L-Lipschitz from the primal ℓ∞ norm to the dual ℓ₁ norm: ‖∇f(x)−∇f(y)‖₁ ≤ L‖x−y‖∞ for all x,y.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/SeparableNoiseLinfSmooth.lean, spec.admissible (coordinate displacement bound and sum of absolute gradient differences).

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: The domain is ℝᵈ with L>0, S≥0, ε>0, and 2³⁰ε² ≤ LΔ. Writing K=(LΔ/ε²)(1+S²/ε²), the dimension must satisfy d ≥ 2¹⁶⁸(1+K)¹⁶.

accuracy.label: gradient_norm
accuracy.details: The algorithm returns one measurable point X in ℝᵈ. Its stationarity measure is the unsquared ℓ₁ norm ‖∇f(X)‖₁ = ∑ᵢ |∂ᵢf(X)|. The output may be any point computed from the final state.

accuracy.label: expected
accuracy.details: The gradient norm at the output must be integrable and satisfy 𝔼‖∇f(X)‖₁ ≤ ε under the joint law of the algorithm and oracle seeds.

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: The setup pairs ℓ∞-to-ℓ₁ gradient smoothness with a pointwise budget on the sum of coordinate noise standard deviations. It measures stationarity in the dual ℓ₁ norm and imposes an explicit dimension threshold tied to accuracy and noise.

descriptionHtml:
High-Dimensional Stationarity with Separable Noise

We seek a stationary point of a differentiable, possibly nonconvex objective f:Rd→R in high dimension d. Its gradient is L-Lipschitz from ℓ∞ to ℓ1, with L>0, and the given starting point x0 lies at most Δ above the finite infimum in objective value. At each query, the oracle uses a fresh independent real sample to return an unbiased gradient estimate whose coordinate standard deviations sum to at most S≥0. For tolerance ε>0, the goal is an output x¯∈Rd satisfying E∥∇f(x¯)∥1≤ε over algorithm and oracle randomness.

The optimization problem is infx∈Rdf(x). The algorithm receives d,L,S,Δ,ε and x0∈Rd. The dimension d∈N and the real parameters satisfy 230ε2≤LΔ,d≥2168(1+LΔε2(1+S2ε2))16.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Smoothness and initial gap). The function f is differentiable everywhere. Its Euclidean gradient satisfies ∥∇f(x)−∇f(y)∥1≤L∥x−y∥∞,x,y∈Rd. The infimum f⋆=infx∈Rdf(x) is finite and satisfies f(x0)−f⋆≤Δ.

Assumption 2 (Stochastic gradients with separable noise). On call k, a query at any x∈Rd returns g(x,ξk), where g:Rd×R→Rd is jointly measurable. The real random variables (ξk)k≥0 are independent with common law ν, and the sequence is independent of the algorithm’s randomness. For ξ∼ν and each fixed x, the vector g(x,ξ) is Bochner integrable. Writing ei(x,ξ)=gi(x,ξ)−∂if(x), each ei(x,ξ)2 is integrable, and Eξ∼ν[g(x,ξ)]=∇f(x),∑i=1dEξ∼ν[ei(x,ξ)2]≤S.

After the allotted oracle calls, the output x¯ must be measurable under the joint law of the algorithm’s randomness and the oracle samples. Its gradient norm ∥∇f(x¯)∥1 must be integrable under this law and satisfy E[∥∇f(x¯)∥1]≤ε.

theorems.referencesHtml:
• Ruichen Jiang, Devyani Maladkar, and Aryan Mokhtari. Provable Complexity Improvement of AdaGrad over SGD: Upper and Lower Bounds in Stochastic Non-Convex Optimization. 2025 (COLT). Complexity: Ω(LΔ/ε2+LΔS2/ε4) stochastic gradient calls for constant-step SGD in the one-dimensional specialization, for E[mint≤T|f′(xt)|]≤ε and ε<cLΔ with universal c>0.
  • Hongyi Tao, Dingzhi Yu, and Lijun Zhang. When and Why SignSGD Outperforms SGD: A Theoretical Study Based on ℓ₁-norm Lower Bounds. 2026 (arXiv v1). Complexity: Ω(LΔ/ε2+LΔS2/ε4) individual stochastic gradient calls for constant-step minibatch SignSGD to attain E[min0≤t<T∥∇f(xt)∥1]≤ε, with S=∑iσi for coordinate standard-deviation bounds σi and BT calls for T steps of batch size B.
theorems.formulaHtml: ⌊L⋅Δ⋅(1+S2ε2)260⋅ε2⌋+

comparisonHtml:
On Rd, f(x0)−inff≤Δ and ∥∇f(x)−∇f(y)∥1≤L∥x−y∥∞. Each gradient query uses a fresh IID real sample. The jointly measurable reply g(x,ξ) is unbiased with finite coordinate variances and ∑iVar(gi(x,ξ))≤S at every x. For L,ε>0, S≥0, A=LΔ/ε2≥230 and d≥2168[1+A(1+S2/ε2)]16, the target is E∥∇f(x^)∥1≤ε for a measurable output of a randomized gradient-only algorithm.

Necessary stochastic gradient calls for high-dimensional ℓ∞-smooth optimization with separable noise.
Result Oracle complexity Novelty Limitations
(1) SeparableNoiseLinfSmoothLowerBound (Ours) (⋆⋆⋆) (review) Lower bound: Ω(A(1+S2/ε2))
(2) SignSGD (Tao et al. 2026, Thm. 2) Lower bound: Ω(A(1+∥σ∥12/ε2)) samples, counting every batch member. Best iterate in expectation: Emint<T∥∇f(xt)∥1. (1) extends hardness to every randomized method and arbitrary output. Under the stated dimension and gap conditions, minibatch SignSGD attains the pointwise-noise minimax rate up to constants. (2) uses fixed coordinate caps Var(gi(x,ξ))≤σi in any dimension. (1) leaves all-method hardness under these caps open and requires A≥230.
(3) Euclidean stationarity (Arjevani et al. 2022, Thm. 3, Eq. (23)) Lower bound: Ω(Aσ2/ε2) single-point value-and-gradient queries for σ>0, ε≤cLΔ. (1) transfers Euclidean hardness to ℓ1 stationarity with separable noise. Direct norm conversion can inflate smoothness by D and noise scale by D in dimension D. (1) covers gradient-only access and requires a larger dimension. (3) allows exact values with each noisy gradient. The geometries preclude direct rate comparison.
(4) Matrix stationarity (Zhang and Lin 2026, Thm. 3.1) Lower bound at p=2: Ω(rAu2) for randomized gradient-only methods. (1) treats vector separable noise. (4) uses spectral-to-nuclear smoothness and nuclear-norm noise and stationarity. Rates are incomparable. (1) requires finite variances. (4) covers 1<p≤2. At p=2, ε≤cmin(LΔ,σ) and M≥CAlog⁡[(2+A)(2+u)].
(5) Matrix stationarity (Hübler et al. 2026, Thm. 3.7) Lower bound at p=2: Ω(ru2) for randomized methods, r≥2. (1), (5): rates are incomparable under separable vector noise and nuclear-norm matrix noise. (5) also covers 1<p<2 for ε<min(σ/4,LΔ/2).
(6) Matrix stationarity (Hübler et al. 2026, Thm. E.9) Lower bound at p=2: Ω(rAu2) for zero-respecting methods, M/r≥A. (1) covers unrestricted randomized methods in vector geometry. The matrix rate in (6) is incomparable. (6) also covers 1<p<2 for ε≤min(σ,LΔ)/300.

Abbr: A=LΔ/ε2, u=σ/ε. In (3), σ2 bounds mean squared Euclidean noise. In (4)–(6), r=min(m,n) and M=max(m,n) for m×n matrices, and σ bounds the Lp norm of the nuclear norm of the noise. c,C>0 denote universal constants at p=2.

Arjevani, Yossi, Yair Carmon, John C. Duchi, Dylan J. Foster, Nathan Srebro, and Blake Woodworth. 2022. Lower Bounds for Non-Convex Stochastic Optimization. https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.1912.02365.
Hübler, Florian, Thomas Pethick, and Suvrit Sra. 2026. Free Heavy-Tailed Lunch for Muon: A Theoretical Justification of Empirical Success. https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2606.14560.
Tao, Hongyi, Dingzhi Yu, and Lijun Zhang. 2026. When and Why SignSGD Outperforms SGD: A Theoretical Study Based on ℓ1-Norm Lower Bounds. https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2605.06615.
Zhang, Jiayu, and Tianyi Lin. 2026. Tight Complexity of Muon Under Heavy-Tailed Noise. https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2605.18528.

import LongTails.Setups.SeparableNoiseLinfSmooth

open MeasureTheory

namespace LongTails.Setups.HighDimensionalSeparableNoiseLinfSmooth

open OracleTemplate

structure Params where
  d : ℕ
  L : ℝ
  S : ℝ
  Δ : ℝ
  ε : ℝ
  x0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)

noncomputable def toGeneral (q : Params) : LongTails.Setups.SeparableNoiseLinfSmooth.Params where
  d := q.d
  Ω := ℝ
  L := q.L
  S := q.S
  Δ := q.Δ
  ε := q.ε
  x0 := q.x0

abbrev spec : Setup where
  Params := Params
  Public := Params
  Instance q := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin q.d) → ℝ
  Query q := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin q.d)
  Reply q := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin q.d)
  Output q := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin q.d)
  publicInput q := q
  valid q := 0 < q.L ∧ 0 ≤ q.S ∧ 0 < q.ε ∧ 2 ^ 30 * q.ε ^ 2 ≤ q.L * q.Δ ∧
    2 ^ 168 * (1 + q.L * q.Δ * (1 + q.S ^ 2 / q.ε ^ 2) / q.ε ^ 2) ^ 16 ≤ (q.d : ℝ)
  admissible q f O :=
    LongTails.Setups.SeparableNoiseLinfSmooth.spec.admissible (toGeneral q) f O
  successful q f output P :=
    LongTails.Setups.SeparableNoiseLinfSmooth.spec.successful (toGeneral q) f output P

end LongTails.Setups.HighDimensionalSeparableNoiseLinfSmooth
